name: Yvette Tsai
life: “I still remember being asked to spell my surname for a form I couldn't read.” On Wednesday, near the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, Yvette notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I left school for a wage and spent my working life hiding my spelling. I want a result in my own name.
appearance: Yvette is easy to recognize by salt-and-pepper curls and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with one cuff folded back twice, Yvette draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first when listening.
personality: Yvette is good at starting things, dreadful at waiting for them to take effect. Close family can tell how worried Yvette is by the number of tiny errands suddenly being done.
agenda: To receive a result under the full name.
family: Carmen Daniels is Yvette’s half-sibling. Yvette decides what stays off the paper. Carmen brings the paper and a pen. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The rescue hut mural*, Carmen says, “I design signs for low vision. I asked regulars to describe the mural with their eyes closed.”
connections: Rowan Davis. Two workers using different strategies for private reading try the same examination paper.

reactions.situation: An examiner offers to read a question aloud
reactions.response: Yvette asks the learner how they want the question presented before the examiner begins.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Yvette writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.

reactions.response: Yvette agrees on a check-in time and keeps busy somewhere out of sight.
